title: Vitamin D deficiency in chronic hepatitis B across the disease spectrum: association with viral activity rather than hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Tufael, Dr; Siddique, Abu Bakar; Rashid, Md Haroon Or; Mujahid, Mohd Hasan; Nath, Nabil Deb; Debnath, Asim; Akter, Most Farhana; Islam, Md Robiul; Upadhye, Vijay Jagdish
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨慢性乙肝中维生素D缺乏与病毒活动及肝癌的关系，仅含少量VDR/STAT1分子对接的探索性分析，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模核心，方法深度不足。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic liver disease is often associated with vitamin D deficiency. However, the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and HBV disease severity, viral activity, and HCC remains unclear. We evaluated whether vitamin D deficiency is linked to the disease stage and HBV viral activity in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and whether HCC is an independent predictor of vitamin D status. METHODS: This study at Ibn Sina Diagnostic Center, Dhaka, included 510 participants: chronic hepatitis B (CHB, n = 210), liver cirrhosis (LC, n = 150), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC, n = 100), and healthy controls (HC, n = 50). Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and HBV DNA were measured using standard assays and real-time PCR. Group comparisons, regression analyses, and exploratory in silico analyses (STRING PPI and docking with VDR and STAT1) were performed. RESULTS: According to the findings of multivariable analysis, the levels of HBV DNA were found to be independently related to baseline vitamin D status. In contrast to this, the levels of HCC were not found to be independently related after adjustment. Univariate analysis of vitamin D and HBV DNA showed a weak correlation, suggesting the necessity to model for confounders. Enrichment of host-guiding PPI illustrated interferon-associated immune pathways, whereas docking substantiated compatibility of a calcitriol molecule with VDR and STAT1, by context hypothesis generating usefulness. CONCLUSION: Chronic HBV infection suggests that vitamin D status relates more to viral activity in the host immune regulatory milieu than to HCC as an independent determinant. Making a statement about explanatory chronology is the first step.
abstract_zh: 背景：慢性肝病常与维生素D缺乏相关。然而，维生素D缺乏与乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）疾病严重程度、病毒活性及肝细胞癌（HCC）之间的关系仍不明确。我们评估了维生素D缺乏是否与慢性乙型肝炎（CHB）的疾病分期和HBV病毒活性相关，以及HCC是否为维生素D状态的独立预测因子。方法：本研究在达卡伊本西纳诊断中心进行，共纳入510名参与者：慢性乙型肝炎（CHB，n=210）、肝硬化（LC，n=150）、肝细胞癌（HCC，n=100）和健康对照（HC，n=50）。使用标准检测方法和实时PCR测量血清25-羟基维生素D和HBV DNA。进行了组间比较、回归分析及探索性计算机模拟分析（STRING PPI及与VDR和STAT1的对接）。结果：根据多变量分析结果，HBV DNA水平被发现与基线维生素D状态独立相关。相比之下，HCC水平在调整后未被发现独立相关。维生素D与HBV DNA的单变量分析显示弱相关性，提示需要对混杂因素进行建模。宿主导向的PPI富集分析揭示了干扰素相关的免疫通路，而对接分析证实了骨化三醇分子与VDR和STAT1的兼容性，这为假设生成提供了背景性有用性。结论：慢性HBV感染提示，维生素D状态与宿主免疫调节环境中的病毒活性关系更为密切，而非作为HCC的独立决定因素。对解释性时间顺序进行陈述是第一步。
